crossRefs.note: Immediately he made his disciples get into the boat, and to go ahead to the other side, to Bethsaida, while he himself…
“Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon which were done…
The apostles, when they had returned, told him what things they had done. He took them and withdrew apart to a desert…
“Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon which were done…
Now Philip was from Bethsaida, of the city of Andrew and Peter.
These, therefore, came to Philip, who was from Bethsaida of Galilee, and asked him, saying, “Sir, we want to see Jesus.”
Four people came, carrying a paralytic to him.
and ran around that whole region, and began to bring those who were sick, on their mats, to where they heard he was.
Wherever he entered, into villages, or into cities, or into the country, they laid the sick in the marketplaces, and…
having heard the things concerning Jesus, came up behind him in the crowd, and touched his clothes.
Jesus stretched out his hand, and touched him, saying, “I want to. Be made clean.” Immediately his leprosy was cleansed.
He touched her hand, and the fever left her. She got up and served him.
Then he touched their eyes, saying, “According to your faith be it done to you.”

people.name: Bethsaida
people.line: Town where Jesus performed miracles, home of several disciples

translations.web: He came to Bethsaida. They brought a blind man to him, and begged him to touch him.
translations.bsb: When they arrived at Bethsaida, some people brought a blind man and begged Jesus to touch him.
translations.kjv: And he cometh to Bethsaida; and they bring a blind man unto him, and besought him to touch him.
translations.asv: And they come unto Bethsaida. And they bring to him a blind man, and beseech him to touch him.
